rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act – Human Trafficking Ground for Removal
rules.requirement: A tenant (or lessee) may be evicted if the leased premises were used in connection with a human-trafficking offense, or if the tenant knowingly harbored a trafficker or allowed one to occupy the premises for residential purposes. The landlord must bring the eviction action within two years of when the violation ended.
rules.key_value: 2-year statute of limitations on bringing the removal action

coverage_conditions.notes: Applies broadly to residential tenants statewide under the general Anti-Eviction Act (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1), which lists this human-trafficking connection as one of the statutory 'good causes' for eviction; the document excerpt does not include the Act's other listed causes.

rules.interaction: This is one of several statutory 'good cause' grounds under the general Anti-Eviction Act; separate, narrower just-cause rules apply to owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2).
rules.quoted_span: knowingly harbors or harbored a person engaged in human trafficking, or permits or permitted such a person to occupy those premises for residential purposes, whether continuously or intermittently.
rules.conflict_note: Document provides only a fragment of the full statutory list of just causes under N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1; other causes are not reproduced here.

rules.title: Just-Cause Eviction Rules for Owner-Occupied Two- and Three-Family Dwellings
rules.requirement: In owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings, a tenant can only be removed by court order, and only for specific causes: staying after lease expiration, failing to pay rent, disorderly conduct destroying other tenants' peace and quiet, willful destruction/damage, constant violation of written rules, or violating a lease re-entry provision. Required notice to quit varies by tenancy type and cause.
rules.key_value: Notice to quit: none required for nonpayment of rent; 3-day notice for disorderly/destructive/rule-violation causes; 1 month for month-to-month tenancy; 3 months for at-will or year-to-year tenancy

coverage_conditions.notes: Applies specifically to landlord-occupied (owner-occupied) two- and three-family dwellings.

rules.exemptions: Applies only to owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings; larger or non-owner-occupied buildings are covered instead by the general Anti-Eviction Act causes.
rules.interaction: Narrower subset of just-cause grounds than the general Anti-Eviction Act (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1), applicable specifically to small owner-occupied buildings.
rules.quoted_span: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only when a court issues an order for eviction.

rules.title: Penalties for Bad-Faith Owner Move-In / Demolition Evictions
rules.requirement: If a landlord evicts a tenant on the ground of wanting to personally occupy the unit, the landlord must actually occupy it for at least six months, or else owes the former tenant treble damages plus attorney fees and costs. If a landlord evicts a tenant to permanently board up, demolish, or retire a building from residential use, the landlord cannot return any unit to residential use for five years, or else owes treble damages, attorney fees/costs, and a civil penalty of up to $10,000 per violation, and the property cannot be registered as a planned real estate development during that five-year period.
rules.key_value: 6-month personal-occupancy requirement; 5-year residential-use restriction after demolition/retirement notice; civil penalty up to $10,000 per violation; treble damages plus attorney fees/costs

coverage_conditions.notes: Applies to landlords who evict tenants on stated grounds of personal occupancy or permanent removal of the building from residential use.

rules.interaction: Operates as an anti-fraud backstop to the owner-occupancy and demolition/retirement 'good causes' for eviction under the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.penalty: Treble (3x) damages plus attorney fees and costs; additionally, up to $10,000 civil penalty per violation and a 5-year bar on planned real estate development registration for the demolition/retirement scenario.
rules.quoted_span:
When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the  landlord 
wishes to personally occupy the unit the landlord must occupy the unit for at least six (6) months.

rules.title: Prohibition on Retaliatory (Reprisal) Eviction
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot evict a tenant, substantially alter the lease or its terms, or refuse to renew a lease in reprisal for the tenant exercising certain civil rights, such as enforcing lease or legal rights, making a good-faith health/safety complaint (after first notifying the landlord), or participating in a tenant organization.

coverage_conditions.notes: Applies to all rental properties used for dwelling purposes, including mobile homes.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are excluded from this reprisal protection.
rules.penalty: Tenant may sue the landlord for damages in a civil action.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights

rules.title: Foreclosure Fairness Act – 90-Day Notice Before Eviction After Foreclosure
rules.requirement: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction in New Jersey. Before a tenant can be evicted due to foreclosure, the new owner who purchased the property and wants to personally occupy it as a primary residence must give the tenant a 90-day notice to quit; this notice may be given up to 90 days before an existing lease expires, and tenants with longer remaining leases cannot be evicted until the lease ends and the 90-day notice has also been given.

coverage_conditions.notes: Applies to residential tenants in properties undergoing or following foreclosure.

rules.exemptions: Month-to-month tenants and tenants in owner-occupied two- and three-family units are NOT exempt from the 90-day notice requirement.
rules.interaction: Supplements, and does not preempt, any State or local law providing longer notice periods or additional tenant protections in foreclosure; federal foreclosure law likewise does not preempt such State/local protections.
rules.quoted_span:
Before a tenant can be evicted due 
to foreclosure, the landlord must provide the tenant with a 90 -day notice to qui t when the 
foreclosed property has been purchased by a buyer who wants to personally occupy it as his or her 
primary residence.

rules.title: Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act
rules.requirement: Qualifying senior citizens (62+ before conversion recording), permanently disabled persons, or disabled veterans (60%+ service-connected disability) who have lived in a building being converted to a condominium, cooperative, or fee-simple ownership for at least one year before the conversion recording may be protected from eviction for up to 40 years, provided their household income does not exceed the greater of three times the county average per-person income or $50,000.
rules.key_value: Up to 40 years protected tenancy; income cap = greater of 3x county average per-person income or $50,000

coverage_conditions.notes: Applies to buildings being converted to condominium, cooperative, or fee-simple ownership; tenant must have resided in the building at least 1 year prior to the conversion recording date.

rules.exemptions: Tenants in Hudson County who do not qualify under this Act may be eligible for additional protected tenancy under the separate Tenant Protection Act of 1992.
rules.interaction: Applications for protected tenancy generally must be filed within 60 days, though later filings may be accepted for good reason if conversion has not yet occurred; a related Tenant Protection Act of 1992 extends similar protection in Hudson County to tenants who do not qualify under this Act.
rules.quoted_span:
Tenants may be protected from eviction for 40 years 
if their family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their 
county or $50,000.00, whichever  is greater

rules.title: Good-Cause Eviction Protections for Rooming and Boarding House Residents
rules.requirement: Owners of rooming and boarding houses must follow the same good-cause and notice requirements as the general Eviction Law when evicting residents, unless the Department's Bureau of Rooming and Boarding House Standards orders otherwise.

coverage_conditions.notes: Rooming or boarding house: a building with at least two living units occupied by unrelated persons without private kitchens and bathrooms (N.J.S.A. 55:13B-3), subject to statutory exceptions (e.g., hotels with more than 85% temporary occupancy, school/college dormitories, buildings housing only college students, certain disability residences).

rules.exemptions: Bureau of Rooming and Boarding House Standards may order otherwise; statutory exceptions under the Rooming and Boarding House Act (hotels with >85% temporary occupancy, dormitories, certain residences for the disabled) remove a building from 'rooming/boarding house' status entirely.
rules.interaction: Incorporates by reference the good-cause and notice requirements of the general Eviction Law (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1 et seq.); also requires at least 3 working days' notice to the County Welfare Board before starting an eviction action for any resident (N.J.A.C. 5:26-3.4(c)).
rules.quoted_span:
require owners of rooming and boarding houses to follow the good causes and notice requirements 
of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau
